challenged_statement: The bare three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis forces some nonzero physical scalar pivot whose Schur residual contains a disjoint 2x2 cross block with determinant large enough for a dimension-free square-plus-cross2 certificate.
counterexample_family: A_m=[1] direct_sum J_m/m direct_sum (-J_m/m), m>=2, spectrum {1,1,-1} plus zeros. Singleton pivot has best invertible disjoint cross2 determinant 1/m^2; every bank pivot has all such determinants zero.
not_refuted: The QFORM conjecture itself; the same family is controlled by grouped-bank aggregation. Also not refuted: the proved square-plus-cross2 sufficient theorem when its determinant hypothesis holds.
